thread:
incident_bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall for GreatLakes region - elevated 5xx and proxy timeouts detected. Incident ID GL-2025-03. Auto-escalation to #incidents.
Jamie SRE: seeing spike in 502/504 from greatlakes-edge-proxies, started ~03:42 UTC. 95p latency jumped to ~9s. Rolling error rate ~7% for the region.
Alex (oncall): acknowledging, I'm on it. putting a quick note in the runbook. Anyone saw recent deploys to edgepool-greatlakes?
Tara - eng-runtime: No infra deploys in the last hour from runtime side. We did push a tiny config change to traffic-router earlier today but it was region-scoped and marked safe.
Mike - netops: BGP and transit look fine. No large network blips. I can confirm healthcheck failures against a subset of edge nodes.
Jamie SRE: grabbing logs. initial hypothesis: an upstream proxy health-check flap + slow KV backend causing backend timeouts to propagate as 5xx at gateway.
Emily - support: we've had 3 customer tickets in the last 15 min mentioning timeouts. Notified two customers with mitigation steps.
Dan - product: impact to latency-sensitive customers is high. Any ETA on mitigation? Need to know if we should alert sales.
Alex (oncall): quick mitigation plan: 1) divert new traffic for GreatLakes to fallback region (ca-central-1) for non-data-resident tenants, 2) increase retry budget and enable quick circuit-breaker on edgepool nodes showing >30% 5xx, 3) scale up edgepool-greatlakes if possible.
Tara - eng-runtime: I can flip the routing policy to prefer ca-central-1 for region-tagged traffic. Doing canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% staged over 6 minutes.
Jamie SRE: running quick queries to identify failing variants:
```
# top failing proxies
cat /var/log/edgepool-greatlakes/proxy.log | jq -r '.proxy_id + " " + .status' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
```
Found 4 proxies with disproportionate failure rates: gl-proxy-05..08.
Mike - netops: I'll start draining gl-proxy-05 and gl-proxy-06 from the pool. Marking them unhealthy in LB.
Alex (oncall): set circuit-breaker to short-circuit on the remaining ones: 10s timeout, 2 failed attempts, 60s cooldown. OpsBot: please apply.
OpsBot: executed: set-circuit-breaker --region greatlakes --timeout 10s --failures 2 --cooldown 60s.
Jamie SRE: after drain/start of reroute, error rate dropped to ~2% in 6 minutes; 95p latency down to 1.2s. But still seeing residual 502s for a subset of tenants pinned to data-residency.
Emily - support: collecting cust IDs impacted by data-residency. forwarding list to Alex.
Dan - product: for data-residency customers we need an explicit fallback policy. Are we allowed to failover them?
Alex (oncall): we cannot silently move data-residency tenants. For those, we need to do targeted remediation: patch failing proxies or escalate to private infra.
Tara - eng-runtime: digging into logs for gl-proxy-07/08. I see a pattern of slow KV lookups; tail latency from KV service spiked from 60ms to >3s correlating with higher request queues on the proxies.
Jamie SRE: is KV service in same region or cross-region?
Tara - eng-runtime: KV is zonal in greatlakes but replicates async. Looks like the local KV node is overloaded.
Mike - netops: possible causes: sudden cache miss storm or background compaction on KV. I'm checking metrics.
OpsBot: KV-cluster-greatlakes alerted: write stalls > 400ms across 3/5 nodes.
Jamie SRE: ok, mitigation path for data-residency tenants: 1) roll a quick restart of KV node to clear compaction, 2) if that fails, promote read-only replica in ca-central-1 temporarily (requires product approvals).
Alex (oncall): Tara, can you coordinate a rolling restart of the offending KV pods? Keep it one at a time and monitor replication lag.
Tara - eng-runtime: starting rolling restart now for kv-greatlakes-1 -> kv-greatlakes-2 sequence. Watch logs.
Jamie SRE: while that's happening, increase proxy retry budget to 3 for requests with idempotent endpoints to smooth transient KV spikes.
Mike - netops: drained gl-proxy-05/06 successfully. gl-proxy-07 still serving but under observation.
Emily - support: customer comms drafted: short blurb + ETA 30m for full mitigation. Approve? :thumbsup:
Dan - product: approve. Make sure we call out data-residency caveat.
Tara - eng-runtime: restart step 1 done. kv-greatlakes-1 restarted, no replication lag spike observed. Tail latency immediately improved to ~120ms.
Jamie SRE: nice, aggregate error rate now ~0.4% and trending down. Great.
Alex (oncall): keep routing preference to ca-central-1 for new sessions for 30 mins then start rolling back to normal. We'll keep circuit-breakers active for 15m more.
OpsBot: routing policy updated: greatlakes -> prefer ca-central-1 at 50%. Scheduled rollback at +30m unless manually extended.
Mike - netops: post-mortem checklist: record proxies drained, KV pod restarted, routing change, customer notifications. Any additional ops we should do?
Jamie SRE: capture heap/profile from gl-proxy-07/08 for root cause. Also archive KV logs for time window for post-incident analysis.
Emily - support: updating tickets: affected customers moved to ca-central-1 (if their policies allowed). For data-residency customers, we escalated to engineering and set SLA hold.
Tara - eng-runtime: leaving temporary retry/circuit settings in place for 15 min. Will revert and file a follow-up PR to add automated fallback for KV hotspot detection.
Alex (oncall): final status: majority traffic restored, residual 0.3% errors for pinned tenants. Acting owners: Tara + Mike for follow-up, Jamie to drive postmortem, Emily to close customer comms with final impact. Great job team. :clap:
Jamie SRE: filing incident ticket GL-2025-03 with timeline, metrics, and actions. Will include suggested fixes: improved KV compaction scheduling, proxy health-check tuning, and automated regional fallbacks for non-data-resident tenants.
Dan - product: please include guidance for sales/support on when we can perform cross-region failover for customers with compliance needs.
Alex (oncall): handing back to normal ops. oncall cleared.
incident_bot: Incident GL-2025-03 resolved (partial). Duration 00:39. Logged actions to postmortems/GL-2025-03.json.
